natural_body: Price-sensitive SMBs: 40% off drove signup +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and we have strong durable evidence that simplification and shortening onboarding improve both completion rates and early adoption. Memory_31 showed signup simplification improved SMB activation, and memory_86 showed shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value. We're verifying both to confirm their magnitude and any boundary conditions before scaling. Activation messaging (memory_91) showed complementary benefits. This addresses the immediate metric decline without the revenue-retention trade-off risk evident in promotional pricing (memory_73: -12% retention despite +18% revenue). Referral incentives and enterprise sales assist are viable but less directly address our current activation/completion declines. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding preserves optionality on pricing response to competition while building on proven, lower-risk levers. The primary risk is modest: if simplification cannibalizes feature discovery, it could affect long-term retention, but prior work suggests the opposite.
